title: Why Porcelain Is Literally Called "China" — Fired at 1,300°C | China Travel Expert
description:
Ever notice your fine teacup and a whole country share one word — "china"?

True porcelain is fired near 1,300°C until the clay vitrifies into a glass-hard, translucent body you can hold light through. Its secret ingredient is kaolin — "china clay" — named after the village of Gaoling beside Jingdezhen, which supplied imperial kilns for over 1,000 years. When Ming voyages carried Jingdezhen blue-and-white across the seas, the ware became the country's name in English.

🧭 Expert Tip: Buying porcelain in Jingdezhen? Tap the rim — real high-fired porcelain rings like a bell and holds the note; a dull thud means a hairline crack.
